attributes.title: How to read chain risk
attributes.visState:
{"title":"How to read chain risk","type":"markdown","aggs":[],"params":{"markdown":"**Latest revision per chain.** Filter by `data.session_id`, source, target or account. Risk is an operational priority, not attack probability. 

**Risk policy:** 40: scan; 65: password guessing; 85: login after failures; +10 with preceding scan (cap 95). Medium 40-69; High 70-100. ATT&CK IDs are candidates from observed evidence. Compromise remains unconfirmed. The history below contains updates, not additional attacks.

**Investigate:** filter one `data.chain_id`. In **Chain evidence**, expand the left arrow and read `data.chain_stage_details`, `data.activity`, `data.attack_chain_json` and `data.evidence_file` in Table/JSON. This preserves full text when a table cell is shortened. A scan has one stage; login does not prove command execution or C2. Optional chain-extended adds fixed shell and verified benign-file probes in the same SSH connection; this is controlled lab instrumentation, not general endpoint auditing. 

[ATT&CK techniques](https://attack.mitre.org/) · [Attack Flow](https://github.com/center-for-threat-informed-defense/attack-flow) · [Wazuh ATT&CK integration](https://documentation.wazuh.com/current/user-manual/ruleset/mitre.html)","fontSize":12,"openLinksInNewTab":true}}
